english.title: Breach safeguards relating to examination of material regarding third party BPD warrant
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section226ID of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
in reliance on a third party BPD warrant
examined
data contained in a third party BPD
knowing/believing
that the examination was in breach of section 226ID(2) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016
deliberately examined the data in breach of that requirement

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The requirement in section 226ID(2) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 is that the examination of the data is necessary and proportionate.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 226ID(4).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 1 to the Interpretation Act 1978 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
